sag-aftra-tvt-2023-employment-based-repl.title: 2023 TV/Theatrical: employment-based digital replicas
sag-aftra-tvt-2023-employment-based-repl.summary: Applies when a covered production creates or uses a digital replica of a performer it employs (voice or likeness in material the performer did not actually perform).

evidence.text: Signed/initialed digital replica consent rider with the use description, linked to the shot/asset IDs it covers
Notice timestamp showing 48-hour notice for scan/capture sessions
Mapping of replica-generated shots to the consented project and use description
Payment calculation records for replica-generated scenes

sag-aftra-tvt-2023-independent-replica-a.title: 2023 TV/Theatrical: independently created replicas and digital alteration
sag-aftra-tvt-2023-independent-replica-a.summary: Applies when a replica of a performer is made without an employment arrangement (e.g. from existing footage) and gives the impression it is that performer, or a performer's recorded performance is digitally altered beyond routine post.

evidence.text: Classification of each AI alteration as routine post (exempt) or beyond script/performance (consent needed)
Source-material provenance for any replica built from existing footage
Consent document or estate/union authorization

sag-aftra-tvt-2023-synthetic-performers.title: 2023 TV/Theatrical: synthetic performers
sag-aftra-tvt-2023-synthetic-performers.summary: Applies when a covered production uses a fully AI-generated, realistic human character in place of a human performer.

evidence.text: Record of union notice for synthetic human characters
Prompt/reference-image log showing no real performer's features were used to generate the character (or consent if they were)

sag-aftra-tvt-2026.title: 2026 TV/Theatrical Agreement AI terms
sag-aftra-tvt-2026.summary: Applies when a SAG-AFTRA-covered film/TV/streaming production scans performers or background actors, makes or uses digital replicas (including from the picture's own footage), digitally alters performances, dubs with a replica, uses a generative-AI 'Synthetic' in a human role, or licenses covered performances for AI training.

evidence.text: Scan-request record with the stated business reason, consent, and the performer's or background actor's identity
Replica asset register: source footage or scan, creation date, holder, people with access, access log, and security measures
Transfer record for any replica that changes hands, with union approval and the transferee's written undertaking
Consent records tied to each replica use, including dubbing consents for pictures starting principal photography on or after 2027-07-01
The script version (and date given to the performer) used to judge whether an alteration was within what was scripted
Flag on any replica or shot involving a minor, with confirmation that no nude or sexual depiction (including age-shifting) was generated
Synthetic-use file: union notice, bargaining record, and the 'significant additional value' justification per role
Record that biometric identifiers were not used outside the picture
Union notice and license record for any sale of performance data for AI training

sag-aftra-commercials-2025.title: 2025 Commercials Contracts (incl. Audio) AI terms
sag-aftra-commercials-2025.summary: Applies when a union commercial creates or uses a performer's digital replica, uses synthetic performers, or uses performer data.

evidence.text: Digital Replica Rider per performer per spot, with use description
MPU tracking and replica destruction/retention records
Access log for stored replica assets (LoRAs, voice models, scans)
Statement that performer footage was not used for model training, or union consent
Synthetic-performer usage report for P&H calculation

sag-aftra-interactive-media-2025.title: 2025 Interactive Media Agreement AI terms
sag-aftra-interactive-media-2025.summary: Applies when a covered game uses vocal or visual digital replicas of performers, or independently created replicas (including prompting a model with a performer's name).

evidence.text: Consent rider with real-time and sensitive-content disclosures
Generated-line counts per performer replica
90-day usage report

wga-mba-ai.title: WGA MBA AI provisions (2023, carried into 2026)
wga-mba-ai.summary: Applies when AI-generated text is given to a covered writer, or a writer uses AI, or literary material is licensed for AI training.

evidence.text: Record of which scripts, treatments or prompts handed to writers were AI-generated, and the disclosure given
Company AI-use policy and any consent given to writers
Note: prompt text used in image/video workflows is not literary material under the MBA, but keep authorship records for scripts

dga-ai.title: DGA Basic Agreement AI terms (2023 and 2026)
dga-ai.summary: Applies when generative AI is used on creative elements of a DGA-covered production.

evidence.text: Record that the director (or other DGA-covered employee) was consulted on each generative-AI creative element, with date and outcome
Director or approver identity attached to each AI-generated shot's workflow history, showing the director's control over that footage
Record of any licensing of production footage for AI training

ampas-99th-oscars-ai-rules.title: 99th Oscars eligibility rules on generative AI
ampas-99th-oscars-ai-rules.summary: Applies when a film using generative AI is submitted for Academy Awards.

evidence.text: Per-shot record of generative AI use and the human contributions (direction, selection, compositing, paint)
Performer consent records for any AI-modified performance
Per-shot list of AI tools used in camera or image work, ready for a Cinematography branch disclosure request

usco-part2-copyrightability.title: Copyright and AI, Part 2: Copyrightability
usco-part2-copyrightability.summary: Applies when a studio wants copyright protection in content that contains AI-generated material.

evidence.text: Human-made inputs per shot: plates, paintovers, 3D layouts, sketches, control maps, with author IDs
Record of human modifications after generation (comp, paint, roto, grading) with before/after versions
Selection and arrangement decisions (which takes were chosen and why, the edit)
Prompt and seed history, which shows process but is not by itself evidence of authorship

usco-registration-ai-disclosure.title: Registration guidance for works containing AI-generated material
usco-registration-ai-disclosure.summary: Applies when a studio registers a work (film, spot, artwork) containing more than de minimis AI-generated material.

evidence.text: Inventory of AI-generated portions per work, enough to write the Material Excluded statement
Description of human-authored contributions per work

thaler-v-perlmutter.title: Thaler v. Perlmutter
thaler-v-perlmutter.summary: Applies when a work is claimed with an AI system as author or with no human authorial contribution.

evidence.text: Identify human authors for every protected deliverable

eu-ai-act-art50-2-provider-marking.title: AI Act Art. 50(2): machine-readable marking of synthetic output
eu-ai-act-art50-2-provider-marking.summary: Applies when the studio is a provider of a generative AI system whose synthetic audio, image, video or text output is used in the EU. Under the Commission's Art. 50 guidelines, a company is a provider if it develops a generative system (or has one developed) and places it on the market or puts it into service under its own name, including for its own in-house use. A company that modifies an existing generative system (e.g. with new training data) and puts it into service under its own name also becomes a provider. Free and open-source model components that are not themselves an AI system are outside Art. 50, but open-source AI systems are not exempt.

evidence.text: Whether the studio acts as a provider (own or modified generative system put into service under its name, including in-house) or only as a deployer of third-party tools, with the reasoning
Per output: whether it is a final deliverable or a closed-loop intermediate inside the production pipeline
Per AI operation: classification as standard editing (exempt) or substantive alteration (marking required), referencing the guidelines' examples
Marking method applied per final output (signed metadata / C2PA manifest, watermark), and verification that it survives the delivery pipeline
Vendor contract terms guaranteeing marking by upstream system providers

eu-ai-act-art50-4-deployer-deepfake.title: AI Act Art. 50(4): deepfake disclosure by deployers
eu-ai-act-art50-4-deployer-deepfake.summary: Applies when a studio, under its own authority, uses an AI system to generate or manipulate image, audio or video that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear authentic (a deepfake, Art. 3(60)), and the content is used in the EU. A deployer established outside the EU is covered where it directs or authorises distribution in the EU (including posting on the globally accessible internet), but not where content reaches the EU through unforeseeable channels outside its control. A client that merely commissions content without deciding or controlling whether and how AI is used is not a deployer; the vendor that does decide is.

evidence.text: Per-deliverable flag: contains a realistic AI-generated or manipulated depiction of real-seeming persons, places or events (Y/N), with the reasoning (VFX/background vs. digital replica, de-aging, synthetic performer)
Whether the evidently-artistic/fictional regime was relied on, and why (format, distribution context, audience expectations)
Disclosure method and placement used (on-screen icon, opening notice, end credits, spoken disclaimer) and the territories where the work was distributed
Contract terms with distributors that keep the label displayed at first exposure
Consent and rights clearances for real persons depicted

eu-code-of-practice-ai-content-transpare.title: Code of Practice on Transparency (marking and labelling) of AI-generated content
eu-code-of-practice-ai-content-transpare.summary: Applies when a provider or deployer wants a recognized way to show Art. 50(2)/(4) compliance.

evidence.text: Whether the studio (and each tool vendor) is a Code signatory
Labelling SOP and record of the label/icon applied per deliverable, with placement and repetition for long-form video
Provenance metadata retained through delivery
Training/awareness records for staff who approve labelling, and the channel for correcting labels

eu-ai-act-art14-human-oversight.title: AI Act Art. 14: human oversight (high-risk systems only)
eu-ai-act-art14-human-oversight.summary: Applies only when the AI system is high-risk (Annex I products or Annex III uses such as biometrics, employment, education, law enforcement, essential services, justice/elections); creative content generation is not an Annex III area.

evidence.text: Classification memo showing the creative pipeline is not a high-risk use
Separate review if AI is used in casting/hiring decisions (employment area)

eu-cjeu-originality-standard.title: Originality = author's own intellectual creation (Infopaq C-5/08; Painer C-145/10; Mio/konektra C-580/23 & C-795/23)
eu-cjeu-originality-standard.summary: Applies when a studio claims copyright in AI-assisted content in an EU member state.

evidence.text: Records of human creative choices visible in the final frame: composition, framing, lighting, layout, paintovers, edit decisions
Link between those choices and the output (e.g. control images, masks, comp scripts)
Contemporaneous documentation of the creative decision process (commentary on Mio/konektra recommends this)

de-ag-munich-ai-logos-2026.title: AG Munich 142 C 9786/25: AI-generated logos not protected
de-ag-munich-ai-logos-2026.summary: Applies when a studio relies on prompting (even long or iterated prompts) to claim copyright in AI output in Germany.

evidence.text: Full prompt and iteration history, together with evidence that specific human choices determine specific visual features
Human-made inputs and edits beyond selection (sketches, layouts, paintovers)

cz-prague-municipal-court-ai-image.title: Prague Municipal Court 10 C 13/2023: AI image not a work
cz-prague-municipal-court-ai-image.summary: Applies when a claimant asserts authorship of a text-to-image output in Czechia.

evidence.text: Contemporaneous, verifiable records linking prompt, settings and output (the claimant lost partly for lack of such proof)

de-gema-v-openai.title: GEMA v OpenAI (42 O 14139/24)
de-gema-v-openai.summary: Applies when a model memorizes and reproduces protected works in outputs.

evidence.text: Model/checkpoint identity and provenance per shot (which provider is responsible)
Output similarity checks against known third-party IP for final deliverables

de-kneschke-v-laion.title: Kneschke v LAION (5 U 104/24)
de-kneschke-v-laion.summary: Applies when training datasets are built from scraped images (relevant if a studio builds training sets for LoRAs or fine-tunes).

evidence.text: Training-data provenance and licence/opt-out checks for any studio-trained LoRA or fine-tune

uk-cdpa-s9-3-computer-generated-works.title: CDPA s9(3) computer-generated works and the 2026 Copyright and AI report
uk-cdpa-s9-3-computer-generated-works.summary: Applies when a work is generated by computer with no human author and protection is claimed in the UK.

evidence.text: Who made the arrangements (producer/operator) for each generated asset, in case s9(3) is relied on
Human-authorship records, which are safer given the proposed repeal

cn-ai-content-labeling-measures.title: Measures for Labeling AI-Generated Synthetic Content
cn-ai-content-labeling-measures.summary: Applies when AI-generated or synthesized content is provided or published through services in China (providers, platforms, and users who publish).

evidence.text: Explicit labels and implicit metadata present on deliverables released in mainland China
Platform declaration records for published content
Record of any vendor (e.g. Chinese GenAI service) user-agreement terms that shift labelling duties to the studio

cn-li-v-liu-beijing-internet-court.title: Li v Liu (Stable Diffusion image)
cn-li-v-liu-beijing-internet-court.summary: Applies when copyright is claimed in AI-generated images in China.

evidence.text: Full prompt, negative prompt, parameter and iteration history showing the user's choices and refinements
Record of the specific model (here Stable Diffusion) and settings used, so the generation process can be explained if challenged

us-ca-ab2602-digital-replica-contracts.title: AB 2602: unenforceable digital replica contract terms
us-ca-ab2602-digital-replica-contracts.summary: Applies when a personal/professional services contract (for new performances fixed on or after 2025-01-01) lets the producer use a digital replica in place of work the individual would otherwise do in person.

evidence.text: Contract clause with a reasonably specific use description
Proof of counsel or union representation
Map of replica-generated shots to the contracted uses

us-ca-ab1836-deceased-personality-replic.title: AB 1836: digital replicas of deceased personalities
us-ca-ab1836-deceased-personality-replic.summary: Applies when a production creates or distributes a digital replica of a deceased personality's voice or likeness in an audiovisual work or sound recording.

evidence.text: Estate consent, or a documented exemption analysis, for any deceased person's likeness or voice

us-ca-sb942-ai-transparency-act.title: California AI Transparency Act
us-ca-sb942-ai-transparency-act.summary: Applies when a covered provider (anyone who creates or produces a GenAI system publicly accessible in California; SB 1000 removed the 1 million monthly-user threshold) creates or alters image, video or audio; studios are affected mainly as licensees and users of such systems, or as providers if they make their own model publicly accessible.

evidence.text: Licence terms from GenAI vendors, including any licensee-obligation notice received under the Act
Confirmation that pipeline steps (transcodes, conforms, metadata scrubs) do not strip vendor latent disclosures
Record of which provider, system name and version produced or altered each asset

us-tn-elvis-act.title: ELVIS Act (voice and likeness)
us-tn-elvis-act.summary: Applies when a person's name, image, voice (including a simulated voice) or likeness is used commercially without authorization, or a tool whose primary purpose is producing a specific person's likeness or voice is distributed.

evidence.text: Authorization for any sound-alike or look-alike, including AI voices 'in the style of' a person

us-ny-synthetic-performer-ad-disclosure.title: Synthetic performer disclosure in advertising
us-ny-synthetic-performer-ad-disclosure.summary: Applies when an ad producer or creator has actual knowledge that an ad includes a synthetic performer (an AI-created human-like performer not recognizable as a real person).

evidence.text: Per-spot flag for synthetic humans and the disclosure used
Distribution territories (NY)

us-ny-post-mortem-digital-replica.title: Post-mortem right of publicity and deceased-performer replicas
us-ny-post-mortem-digital-replica.summary: Applies when a deceased personality's name, voice, likeness etc. is used commercially, or a deceased performer's digital replica is used in an audiovisual work, sound recording or live music.

evidence.text: Rights-holder consent, or an exemption analysis

us-ny-gol-5-302-digital-replica-contract.title: New York digital replica contract law
us-ny-gol-5-302-digital-replica-contract.summary: Applies when a personal or professional services contract entered into or modified on or after 2025-01-01 allows a digital replica of the individual's voice or likeness to replace work they would otherwise do in person.

evidence.text: Same as California AB 2602: use description plus proof of representation

us-no-fakes-act.title: NO FAKES Act
us-no-fakes-act.summary: Applies when would apply to unauthorized digital replicas of any individual's voice or visual likeness.

evidence.text: Likeness/voice licences, which already exist under state law practice

us-take-it-down-act.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act
us-take-it-down-act.summary: Applies when nonconsensual intimate imagery, including AI digital forgeries, is published or hosted.

evidence.text: Policy prohibiting sexual/intimate generation of real people without consent; content-review logs

c2pa-content-credentials.title: C2PA Content Credentials + IPTC digital source types
c2pa-content-credentials.summary: Applies when a studio wants machine-readable provenance on deliverables (supports Art. 50, SB 942, China implicit labels, and platform auto-labelling).

evidence.text: Signed manifest per deliverable listing ingredients (plates, generated elements), actions and digitalSourceType
Where used: a c2pa.ai-disclosure assertion naming the model(s) and the human oversight level
Signing certificate/identity used by the studio

youtube-altered-synthetic-disclosure.title: YouTube altered or synthetic content disclosure
youtube-altered-synthetic-disclosure.summary: Applies when realistic AI-generated or altered content is uploaded: real people saying or doing things they didn't, altered real events or places, realistic scenes that didn't happen, or AI music as the focus.

evidence.text: Per-upload disclosure setting and rationale

meta-ai-labels-ads.title: Meta AI disclosure for political/social-issue ads and AI info labels
meta-ai-labels-ads.summary: Applies when ads on Meta platforms are created or edited with GenAI; political, election or social-issue ads contain photorealistic or realistic-sounding digitally created/altered media.

evidence.text: Ad-level AI disclosure flag (required for political/social-issue ads)
The creative's provenance metadata (e.g. C2PA), which may trigger automatic labelling
Record of whether edits were 'significant' (generated backgrounds or images) or minor (resize, colour correction)

us-ftc-reviews-testimonials-rule.title: FTC Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule + AI claims guidance
us-ftc-reviews-testimonials-rule.summary: Applies when an ad uses testimonials or endorsements, including AI-generated people or voices presented as real customers or celebrities, or makes claims about AI.

evidence.text: Record identifying which on-screen 'customers' or endorsers are synthetic, and substantiation that they are not presented as real testimonials

allen-v-perlmutter.title: Allen v. Perlmutter (Théâtre D'opéra Spatial)
allen-v-perlmutter.summary: Applies when a studio seeks US copyright in an image or shot whose expressive content came mainly from iterative prompting of a generative model.

evidence.text: Prompt and iteration logs per generated asset (count, revisions, selections)
Separate before/after versions of human paint/comp edits, so they can be claimed apart from the generated base
Record of upscalers or enhancers used (e.g. Gigapixel AI) and whether they add new content

usco-part3-generative-ai-training.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 3: Generative AI Training (pre-publication)
usco-part3-generative-ai-training.summary: Applies when a studio uses, fine-tunes or trains a model, or relies on a vendor's claim that its training was lawful.

evidence.text: For fine-tunes and LoRAs the studio trains: an inventory of training images and clips with the licence or ownership basis for each
Vendor training-data representations and indemnities for each third-party model used

getty-v-stability-uk.title: Getty Images v Stability AI [2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch)
getty-v-stability-uk.summary: Applies when a UK-produced or UK-exploited deliverable uses Stable Diffusion, or the studio imports or uses model weights trained abroad.

evidence.text: Model name and exact version for each generation (e.g. SD 1.5, SD 2.1, SDXL)
QC record showing outputs were checked for watermarks, logos and signatures

getty-v-stability-us.title: Getty Images v. Stability AI (N.D. Cal.)
getty-v-stability-us.summary: Applies when a US-exploited deliverable uses Stable Diffusion models.

evidence.text: Model name and version per shot
QC for watermarks and logos in outputs
Vendor licence and indemnity terms for Stability models

studios-v-midjourney.title: Disney Enterprises & Universal v. Midjourney; Warner Bros. Entertainment v. Midjourney (consolidated)
studios-v-midjourney.summary: Applies when a shot is generated with Midjourney, or any output depicts or resembles characters owned by these studios or other third parties.

evidence.text: Prompt log screened for third-party character and franchise names
Output review sign-off for resemblance to third-party characters
Model name per generation (Midjourney version)

studios-v-minimax-hailuo.title: Disney Enterprises, Universal & Warner Bros. Discovery v. MiniMax (Hailuo AI)
studios-v-minimax-hailuo.summary: Applies when a shot is generated with MiniMax / Hailuo models, or any output depicts third-party characters.

evidence.text: Model name and version per generation (MiniMax/Hailuo family, via API, partner node or local weights)
Output review sign-off for resemblance to third-party characters
Vendor terms and indemnity for MiniMax use

andersen-v-stability.title: Andersen v. Stability AI, Midjourney, DeviantArt and Runway
andersen-v-stability.summary: Applies when a shot uses Stable Diffusion-based models, Midjourney, DeviantArt's generator or Runway models.

evidence.text: Model and checkpoint per generation, including community fine-tunes derived from Stable Diffusion
Prompt log screened for living artists' names used as style cues

bartz-v-anthropic.title: Bartz v. Anthropic (fair-use ruling and class settlement)
bartz-v-anthropic.summary: Applies when a studio relies on a model whose provider trained on pirated or unlawfully acquired data, or trains its own models.

evidence.text: Provider's statements on how training data was acquired, for each model used
For in-house fine-tunes: proof that the training material was lawfully acquired or licensed

kadrey-v-meta.title: Kadrey v. Meta (Llama training fair-use ruling)
kadrey-v-meta.summary: Applies when a studio relies on Llama-family models, or on any model trained on scraped or pirated works.

evidence.text: Model name and version per use (e.g. Llama variants inside prompt-expansion nodes)
Provider training-data statements

thomson-reuters-v-ross-3d-cir.title: Thomson Reuters v. ROSS Intelligence (No. 25-2153)
thomson-reuters-v-ross-3d-cir.summary: Applies when a studio trains or fine-tunes a model on third-party copyrighted material for a competing commercial purpose.

evidence.text: Purpose and licence basis for each in-house training dataset

cox-v-sony-contributory-liability.title: Cox Communications v. Sony Music Entertainment (No. 24-171)
cox-v-sony-contributory-liability.summary: Applies when assessing who bears infringement risk when a generative service produces infringing output at a user's request.

evidence.text: Output review sign-off covering third-party works and characters
Prompt logs showing the studio did not seek third-party characters

cn-zhangjiagang-butterfly-chairs.title: Feng v. furniture manufacturer ('butterfly chairs' Midjourney images)
cn-zhangjiagang-butterfly-chairs.summary: Applies when copyright is claimed in China in AI images made mainly by prompting.

evidence.text: Full prompt, parameter, seed and iteration history
Record of human modifications to outputs

cn-changshu-half-heart.title: Lin v. inflatable model company ('half heart' Midjourney + Photoshop image)
cn-changshu-half-heart.summary: Applies when copyright is claimed in China in an AI image that the user refined.

evidence.text: Prompt and modification history
Human post-edits (Photoshop/Nuke), with versions
Registration certificate, where available

cn-spc-ai-dispute-opinions-2026.title: Opinions on Adjudicating AI-Related Dispute Cases in Accordance with Law
cn-spc-ai-dispute-opinions-2026.summary: Applies when AI-generated content is exploited in China, or a dispute is heard by Chinese courts.

evidence.text: Prompt logs and reference inputs showing whether a pre-existing work was targeted
Records of output similarity review

ca-cippic-v-sahni.title: CIPPIC v. Sahni (SURYAST registration naming an AI co-author)
ca-cippic-v-sahni.summary: Applies when copyright in an AI-assisted work is claimed or registered in Canada.

evidence.text: Identification of the human author for each deliverable in Canadian filings

jp-chiba-ai-image-referral.title: First Japanese criminal referral treating AI-generated images as protected works
jp-chiba-ai-image-referral.summary: Applies when heavily prompted AI-generated images are used or copied in Japan.

evidence.text: Provenance of any third-party AI image used as a source

eu-commission-art50-guidelines-2026.title: Commission Guidelines on AI Act Art. 50 transparency, C(2026) 5054: film and VFX treatment
eu-commission-art50-guidelines-2026.summary: Applies when a studio produces AI-assisted image, video or audio for distribution in the EU and needs to decide whether outputs must be machine-marked (Art. 50(2)) or labelled as deepfakes (Art. 50(4)).

evidence.text: Per shot: AI operations performed and their classification (standard edit / substantive alteration / generation)
Per deliverable: deepfake assessment (VFX/background vs. replica, de-aging, synthetic performer), and whether the artistic/fictional regime is relied on
Disclosure placement and timing for each distributed version
Which party (studio, vendor, client) decided and controlled the AI use

eu-ai-act-art53-gpai-provider-obligation.title: AI Act Art. 53: general-purpose AI model providers must publish a training-data summary and keep a copyright policy
eu-ai-act-art53-gpai-provider-obligation.summary: Applies when a shot uses a general-purpose AI model (including large image or video generation models trained above about 10^23 FLOP) whose provider places it on the EU market. The obligations fall on the model provider, not on a studio using the model. A studio that modifies a model with compute above one-third of the original training compute becomes a provider for that modification (Commission GPAI guidelines, per commentary).

evidence.text: For each model/checkpoint used in a shot: the provider's identity
Whether the provider publishes a training-data summary on the Commission template (link and date)
Whether the provider publishes a copyright policy (link), and whether it is a GPAI Code of Practice signatory for the Transparency and Copyright chapters
For open-weight or community models: whether the model is above the GPAI threshold and whether any summary/policy exists; flag unknown-provenance fine-tunes and LoRAs
For studio fine-tunes: training compute relative to the base model, and the studio's own dataset records

eu-gpai-code-of-practice.title: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (Transparency, Copyright, Safety & Security chapters): signatory status
eu-gpai-code-of-practice.summary: Applies when a studio wants to show that the providers of models used in its shots follow a recognised route to Art. 53 compliance.

evidence.text: Per model used: provider's signatory status on the Commission list (checked on date X), and which chapters

Signatories listed on 2026-10-07: AI Studio Delta, Aleph Alpha, Almawave, Amazon, Anthropic, Black Forest Labs, Bria AI, Cohere, Domyn, Dweve, Fastweb, Google, IBM, LINAGORA, Microsoft, Mistral AI, Open Hippo, OpenAI, Pleias, Reflection AI, ServiceNow, WRITER, xAI (Safety and Security only)

eu-ai-act-art5-ncii-prohibition.title: AI Act ban on AI systems generating non-consensual intimate imagery or CSAM
eu-ai-act-art5-ncii-prohibition.summary: Applies when a studio's AI system or workflow is used to generate or manipulate realistic intimate or sexually explicit imagery, video or audio of an identifiable person.

evidence.text: Per shot with intimate content: identity of any real person depicted and their explicit written consent covering AI generation/manipulation
Confirmation that body doubles, de-aging or digital replicas in intimate scenes are covered by consent
Model/tool safeguards for any in-house generative system

it-law-132-2025-copyright-ai-assisted-wo.title: Italy AI Law Art. 25: AI-assisted works protected only as human intellectual work; TDM rule
it-law-132-2025-copyright-ai-assisted-wo.summary: Applies when a studio claims copyright in Italy in AI-assisted content, or builds training data from online works.

evidence.text: Records of human creative contribution to each AI-assisted shot
For studio-trained models/LoRAs: lawful-access and opt-out checks for training material

it-penal-612-quater-ai-deepfake.title: Italy: crime of unlawfully disseminating AI-generated or altered content
it-penal-612-quater-ai-deepfake.summary: Applies when AI-falsified or altered images, video or voices of a person are shared or published in Italy without that person's consent.

evidence.text: Consent of each real person whose likeness or voice is AI-generated or altered, covering the specific use and distribution
Disclosure/labelling decisions that bear on whether content could mislead as to genuineness

fr-penal-226-8-ai-montage-consent.title: France: offence to publish AI-generated content of a person without consent unless obviously artificial or labelled
fr-penal-226-8-ai-montage-consent.summary: Applies when AI-generated visual or audio content reproducing a person's image or speech is made public or shared in France.

evidence.text: Consent of each real person whose image or voice is AI-generated
Where consent is absent, the on-screen statement that the content is AI-generated (or why it is obviously artificial)

dk-l49-likeness-imitation-bill.title: Denmark bill L 49: consent required to publish realistic digital imitations of a person's appearance, voice or movements
dk-l49-likeness-imitation-bill.summary: Applies when a production makes available to the public in Denmark a realistic digitally generated imitation of a real person's appearance, voice or movements, or of a performer's performance.

evidence.text: Written consent from each real person or performer whose likeness, voice or performance is digitally imitated, covering Denmark
Consent date and withdrawal handling

de-olg-duesseldorf-ai-comic-2026.title: OLG Duesseldorf I-20 W 2/26: AI comic of a photo neither infringing nor a protected work
de-olg-duesseldorf-ai-comic-2026.summary: Applies when a studio feeds a third-party photo or image into an AI tool as a reference, or claims protection for the AI result, in Germany.

evidence.text: Reference images used as inputs, with their licence/source
Similarity review of output against reference inputs (framing, perspective, lighting retained or not)
Documented creative decisions (prompts, controls, edits) if protection of the output may be claimed

de-gema-v-suno-2026.title: GEMA v Suno: AI music generator liable for storing and outputting songs
de-gema-v-suno-2026.summary: Applies when a production uses an AI music generator whose model may reproduce protected songs in its output.

evidence.text: Which music-generation model/provider produced each cue
Similarity check of generated music against known works before final mix
Licence terms and indemnities from the music-generation provider

fr-ppl-presumption-ai-use-cultural-conte.title: France bill: presumption that AI providers used protected works (burden-of-proof reversal)
fr-ppl-presumption-ai-use-cultural-conte.summary: Applies when rights holders sue AI providers in France over training on protected works; affects the providers of models a studio uses.

evidence.text: For each model used: provider identity and published training-data summary (links to the Art. 53 record)

netflix-genai-production-partner-guidanc.title: Netflix guidance on using generative AI in content production
netflix-genai-production-partner-guidanc.summary: Applies when a production partner or vendor (including VFX and AI studios hired by the production or by Netflix) plans to use GenAI on a Netflix production.

evidence.text: Record that the Netflix contact was notified of GenAI use, with date
Written Netflix approval (or 'not required' rationale) for each escalated use, linked to the shot
Tool and model list per shot, with each tool's data terms (no storage, reuse or training) and whether an enterprise environment was used
Flag for GenAI pixels in the final deliverable versus temp or ideation only
Prompt and reference-input log showing no copyrighted works, public figures or unlicensed likenesses referenced, or the approval if they were
Talent consent records for any replica or performance alteration

mpa-tpn-content-security-ai-controls.title: MPA Content Security Best Practices v5.3.2: AI Supplemental v1.0 (AI/ML controls)
mpa-tpn-content-security-ai-controls.jurisdiction: Global (industry standard; contractual for vendors to MPA member studios)
mpa-tpn-content-security-ai-controls.summary: Applies when a vendor handles content of MPA member studios (Netflix, Paramount, Amazon, Sony Pictures, Universal, Disney, Warner Bros.) or is TPN-assessed, and uses AI/ML tools on client content.

evidence.text: Per-project written client approval of each AI tool or service used on client content
Approved AI tool inventory/SBOM entry for every node pack, model, LoRA and API used, with version, source and approval status
Per-run AI audit log: prompt, model, workflow stage, outputs, operator account, timestamp
Model scan record and checksum for each downloaded model before it entered the content network
Data-handling terms for any third-party AI API (no training, retention period, tenant isolation)
Written client consent if client content was used to train or fine-tune (e.g. a LoRA trained on plates)
Optional: C2PA manifest for deliverables where the client requires it

uk-asa-cap-ai-in-ads.title: UK advertising codes applied to AI-generated content (no blanket AI label)
uk-asa-cap-ai-in-ads.summary: Applies when an ad within ASA remit (non-broadcast under CAP, TV/radio under BCAP) contains AI-generated or AI-altered imagery, voices or people.

evidence.text: Record of whether the ad contains AI-generated people, voices or product depictions, and the disclosure decision with rationale
Substantiation that product depictions are not exaggerated by AI (e.g. untouched reference footage)
Permission records for any real person's likeness or voice
Human review sign-off for bias and social responsibility

eo-insurance-ai-underwriting.title: Errors & omissions insurance: underwriting expectations for AI-assisted content
eo-insurance-ai-underwriting.jurisdiction: Global (insurance market practice; reported for Canada, UK and US)
eo-insurance-ai-underwriting.summary: Applies when a production that carries or needs E&O insurance (typically required by distributors before release) uses GenAI in delivered content.

evidence.text: Per-shot list of AI tools/models used, for the E&O application
Human clearance review sign-off per AI-generated element (who, when, what was checked)
Chain of title for inputs: plates, reference images, LoRA training data, music
Similarity or reverse-image check results for generated elements
The studio's written AI usage policy and the version in force for the shot

us-ca-sb1050-synthetic-performer-ad-disc.title: SB 1050: synthetic performer disclosure in advertising
us-ca-sb1050-synthetic-performer-ad-disc.summary: Applies when a person creates and causes to be published an audio, audiovisual or visual advertisement that prominently features a synthetic performer (a digital human created at least in part with generative AI and not recognizable as any identifiable natural person).

evidence.text: Per-spot flag recording whether a generated human appears and whether it is prominent
The exact disclosure wording and its placement on each California deliverable
For ads promoting a film or series: note that the synthetic performer matches its use in the work

us-ca-civ3344-digital-replicas.title: Living-person right of publicity covers digital replicas
us-ca-civ3344-digital-replicas.summary: Applies when a living person's voice or likeness, including a highly realistic digital replica (also of a performance they never gave or that was materially altered), is knowingly used for advertising, selling or soliciting without consent.

evidence.text: Signed consent or licence for any living person's voice or likeness used in ads or merchandise, including AI replicas
For employee likeness in marketing, a signed release (the presumption no longer applies after 2027-01-01)

us-il-right-of-publicity-digital-replica.title: Illinois Right of Publicity Act: unauthorized digital replicas
us-il-right-of-publicity-digital-replica.summary: Applies when a sound recording or audiovisual work containing a digital replica of a real individual's voice, image or likeness (made with AI or other technology, in a work the person did not perform in) is distributed or made available to the public.

evidence.text: Consent from the depicted individual or rights holder for every real-person replica in a released work
For documentary or biographical uses: note why the replica does not create a false impression of authentic participation

us-il-digital-voice-likeness-contracts.title: Illinois Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (contract terms)
us-il-digital-voice-likeness-contracts.summary: Applies when a personal or professional services agreement entered into after 2024-08-09 allows a digital replica of the individual's voice or likeness to replace work they would otherwise do in person.

evidence.text: Contract clause with a reasonably specific replica-use description
Proof of counsel or union representation
Map of replica-generated shots to the contracted uses

us-wa-forged-digital-likeness.title: Washington personality rights: forged digital likeness
us-wa-forged-digital-likeness.summary: Applies when a realistic AI-created or altered image, video or audio of an identifiable person (a 'forged digital likeness' likely to deceive a reasonable person) is used without consent.

evidence.text: Consent for any real person whose likeness or voice is synthesized
Exemption analysis for satire, parody or commentary uses

ca-copyright-human-authorship.title: Canada: copyright in AI-assisted works requires a human author exercising skill and judgment
ca-copyright-human-authorship.summary: Applies when a studio claims or relies on Canadian copyright in a shot or work that contains AI-generated material.

evidence.text: Record of human creative choices (prompts, edits, selection, compositing) per shot, separate from model output
Names of the human authors per work

ca-criminal-code-sexual-deepfakes.title: Canada: sexual deepfakes added to the non-consensual intimate image offence
ca-criminal-code-sexual-deepfakes.summary: Applies when sexually explicit or near-nude synthetic images of a real person are made available or threatened to be distributed without consent.

evidence.text: Policy prohibiting sexual or intimate generation of real people without consent
Content-review logs for intimate or nude generations

jp-copyright-art30-4-training.title: Japan: AI training under Art. 30-4 and its limits
jp-copyright-art30-4-training.summary: Applies when a studio or vendor trains, fine-tunes (e.g. LoRA) or builds RAG over copyrighted works in Japan.

evidence.text: Dataset manifest for any studio-trained or fine-tuned model (sources, licences, whether a single creator's work dominates)
Record of crawler compliance with robots.txt and access controls

jp-ai-output-infringement-copyrightabili.title: Japan: infringement by AI outputs and copyrightability of AI-assisted works
jp-ai-output-infringement-copyrightabili.summary: Applies when AI-generated material is used, published or sold in Japan, or a studio claims Japanese copyright in it.

evidence.text: Similarity check against known reference works for hero assets
Prompt, iteration and edit history showing human creative contribution
Record of models used and their training-data disclosures

jp-ai-promotion-act.title: Japan AI Promotion Act
jp-ai-promotion-act.summary: Applies when context only: businesses that develop or use AI in Japan.

evidence.text: None specific; monitor guidelines issued under the Act

jp-tsuda-voice-publicity-ruling.title: Tsuda v. TikTok operator: voices protected by publicity rights
jp-tsuda-voice-publicity-ruling.summary: Applies when an AI-generated voice resembling a real performer is used without permission to attract customers or audiences in Japan.

evidence.text: Consent or licence for any voice clone or sound-alike of a real Japanese performer

kr-ai-basic-act-art31-transparency.title: Korea AI Basic Act Art. 31: generative AI notice and labelling
kr-ai-basic-act-art31-transparency.summary: Applies when an AI business operator (developer, or business offering a product or service using AI) provides generative AI products or services or their outputs to users in Korea, including from abroad.

evidence.text: Whether the studio acts as an AI business operator for the deliverable (offering an AI product/service) or only as a user
Labels or watermarks/metadata on AI-generated deliverables released in Korea, and the notice method used for creative works

kr-copyright-registration-genai-guide.title: Korea: Guide to Copyright Registration for Generative AI-Assisted Works
kr-copyright-registration-genai-guide.summary: Applies when a studio registers or relies on Korean copyright in a work containing generative AI output.

evidence.text: Per-work breakdown of AI-generated versus human-created portions
Documentation of the creation process (the guide suggests e.g. screen recordings)

iatse-basic-agreement-2024-ai.title: 2024 IATSE Basic Agreement: Article XLIX Artificial Intelligence
iatse-basic-agreement-2024-ai.summary: Applies when a producer signatory to the IATSE Basic Agreement (Hollywood West Coast studio locals) assigns or allows AI systems in covered crew work, or asks to scan a crew member's visual or vocal likeness.

evidence.text: Copy of the producer's written AI-use policy as given to crew and to the union
Per-shot record of which crew member used which AI system, and the producer's consent where required
Record that the employee disclosed AI use (needed to keep indemnity)
Signed scan-consent form for any crew likeness capture, stating consent is not a condition of employment
Consultation requests and responses where AI use was required

tag-839-2024-ai.title: 2024 Animation Guild Agreement: Article 21.N Artificial Intelligence
tag-839-2024-ai.summary: Applies when a signatory animation producer asks or requires TAG-covered artists, writers or technical staff to use generative AI, provides AI-generated written material to an animation writer, or asks to scan an employee's likeness.

evidence.text: Dated written GenAI notice to each employee on the show or task
Consultation request and outcome, including alternatives considered
Record of AI-generated text supplied to writers and the disclosure given
Producer AI policy and the employee's disclosure of AI use
Scan consent for any employee likeness capture

actra-ipa-2025-ai.title: ACTRA Independent Production Agreement 2025-2027: AI and digital replica terms (Parts G and H)
actra-ipa-2025-ai.summary: Applies when an English-language production under the ACTRA IPA (Canada outside British Columbia, e.g. Toronto or Montreal English-language work) creates or uses digital replicas of performers, background or animation performers, or uses synthetic performers or voices.

evidence.text: Dated replica-creation notice (48 hours) and signed consent per performer, including background and animation performers
Use description attached to each replica asset
Time records for replica-creation sessions
Record of ACTRA negotiation before any synthetic character or voice is used
Upgrade record for background performers altered to speak

ubcp-actra-bcmpa-2025-ai.title: BC Master Production Agreement (2025-2028): AI and digital replica terms
ubcp-actra-bcmpa-2025-ai.summary: Applies when a production under the BC Master Production Agreement (most US studio and Canadian live-action work in British Columbia, e.g. Vancouver) creates or uses performer or background digital replicas, alters performances, or uses synthetic performers.

evidence.text: 48-hour notice and signed consent per performer and background performer
Estimated-days calculation for replica-replaced performance
Background count records showing replicas were not used to meet minimums
Consent and bargaining record for any synthetic built from recognizable features
